note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: The Street's Q4 2026 revenue bar is about $222.6M, only +3.5% q/q on a ~$215M Q3. Management's own forward commentary points above that: on the Q2 call it said there would be no 'stairstep', with optical volumes rising as more customers enter production and visibility of about six months, and Q1-27 orders already being placed. At Citi TMT (scheduled 2026-09-09) it said customer orders/forecasts cover next year, lead times are 26-28 weeks and pricing stays firm through end-2027. The 10-Q shows inventory +35% to $105.5M, with WIP up from $47.6M to $79.0M since December, plus restricted cash tied to purchase obligations. This corroborates a ramp rather than a stall, so a Q4 guide midpoint in the $230-240M area would clear the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide is what moves this name. April 2026: Q2 guide well above Street, +76.1%. July 2026: Q3 guide of $210-220M against ~$175M Street still fell -21.5%, after a ~22% run into the print. So a strong guide has paid once and been sold once. 5 of the last 7 reactions were down.

findings.finding: MXL goes into this print after a sector-driven de-rating rather than a run-up. It is -16.4% over 5 days and -23.4% over 20 days. The cause is a sector-wide sell-off: optical names fell on 10-15 ('rotation into defensives', no company news), and the SOX fell ~12% in the week to 10-14 after Broadcom's Hock Tan and Intel's Lip-Bu Tan said capital, not chips, is AI's constraint, while Hock Tan said demand exceeds supply through 2029. In July, by contrast, the stock ran ~22% into the print and fell 21.5% on a beat-and-raise. No MXL-specific negative 8-K, PR or downgrade appears since July 23 (EDGAR shows only Forms 4/144/13G).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: up ~22% into the print, then -21.5% on beat-and-raise. April 2026: entered depressed and moved +76%. That is two observations consistent with run-in mattering, which is not a base rate.

findings.finding: Optical counterparties that reported after MXL last spoke (2026-07-23) describe continuing strong demand. Credo's FQ1-27 (reported 2026-09-02, quarter ended 2026-08-01) had revenue of $479M (+115% y/y), a record optical DSP quarter and a guide of $525-535M. Eoptolink's H1 report (2026-08-25) had Q2 revenue +50.8% q/q, and brokers cite high Q3/Q4 order visibility. Neither shows an air pocket in 800G module/DSP demand during MXL's Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: MXL has beaten revenue consensus by 0-2.6% in each of the last 6 quarters (MarketBeat), and the reactions to those beats were mostly negative.

findings.finding: The Silicon Motion SIAC arbitration (claim: $160M termination fee plus further damages) has had its hearings concluded (October 2025 and March 2026), and the parties are awaiting a final award. One call summary expected a decision in 2H 2026. MXL had $64.8M of unrestricted cash, a $125M term loan and negative H1 operating cash flow (-$4.1M) at 6/30. An adverse award disclosed in the Q3 release or 10-Q would force a financing question. No award has been reported by either party as of 10-22, so this is a low-probability tail inside the window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There has been no award in the history. The matter has been a disclosed risk factor since 2023.

findings.finding: Every Q3 2026 scenario input printed above the FY scenario Eni used on 29 July to set its EUR15bn CFFO guide and EUR3.4bn buyback (Brent $85, SERM $14, TTF EUR50/MWh): Brent averaged $97.0, TTF averaged $21.5/MMBtu (about EUR63/MWh), and TotalEnergies' European refining marker was $33.2/b against $13.5 in Q2. Brent was still around $100 in mid-October. Eni's published policy pays 100% of the CFFO increment as an extraordinary dividend in Q4 when Brent is above $90 or refining margins are 50%+ above budget, with the decision due 'in October'. Using Eni's own sensitivities (EUR0.11bn per $1 Brent, EUR0.08bn per $1 SERM), FY Brent near $95 and FY SERM near $13-15 give an increment of roughly EUR1.1-1.4bn. The street expects about EUR1bn (Equita) and FY CFFO of about EUR16bn. The Plenitude deconsolidation (completed 1 October) and the $2bn Ares capital expected in Q3 also push gearing below the 10% floor, which supports a buyback upsize on top.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Distribution news has driven the last three prints. Q3 2025: shares rose on a buyback upsize (https://sweetcrudereports.com/eni-ups-buyback-on-strong-q3-results-shares-rise/). Q1 2026: about +1% despite an earnings miss, because the buyback rose to EUR2.8bn (https://www.milanofinanza.it/news/eni-gli-analisti-conti-sotto-le-attese-ma-convincono-il-buyback-a-2-8-miliardi-e-le-stime-sulla-202604241117072364). The baseline's own 8-move history is monthly 6-K noise and was not used.

findings.finding: Peer updates point to a large sequential refining step-up for Eni's Q3. TotalEnergies' European refining marker went from $13.5 to $33.2/b (+146%), with R&C cash flow guided about $2bn higher QoQ, and Shell put Q3 refining margins at a record $42 vs $24. Eni's Q2 SERM was $8.3/b, which earned refining EBIT of EUR80m. Scaling by the peer marker implies a Q3 SERM near $20, worth roughly +EUR0.2bn of quarterly refining EBIT (EUR0.02bn per $1 per quarter). That roughly offsets the Brent drop ($104.5 to $97, about -EUR0.2bn quarterly CFFO), and higher TTF (+EUR0.1bn) is upside to GGP. The Q3 adjusted net bridge from Q2's EUR2.33bn therefore lands around EUR2.45-2.55bn, at or slightly above the EUR2.48bn company consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat consensus by about 11% and the stock rose +4.5% intraday, with the buyback raised the same day. Q1 2026 missed by about 14% (1.3 vs 1.51 per WallStreetItalia) and still rose about 1% on the buyback. The quarter's number has mattered less than distributions.

findings.finding: Direct peer FIBRA Prologis reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-21 after the close, the first Mexican industrial landlord to speak since Vesta's July print. Period-end occupancy rose to 96.5% from 95.8% at Q2. The CEO cited 'improving customer demand and lower construction starts'. Against that, same-store cash NOI was +1.7% vs +14.8% a year earlier, average occupancy 95.1% vs 97.9%, rent change on rollover 36.2% vs 47.2%, and retention 66.0% vs 81.7%. Net, a mildly positive demand read on occupancy direction with decelerating rent momentum.

findings.finding: At the Barclays conference on 2026-09-10, eleven weeks into Q3, CEO Jim Koch said the summer 'did not improve' from Boston Beer's point of view and that the trend 'has not been good'. The last numbers were 29-week depletions at -5%, Q2 at -6%, and a CFO statement in July that current trends point to the low end of the FY volume guide (down low to mid single digits). A third weak quarter puts full-year depletions at or below the low end, which makes a cut or narrowing of the volume guide and a softer 2027 setup likely. Revenue consensus of -2.6% leans on shipments, not depletions.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-04-30: the volume guide was narrowed down (from flat-to-down-mid to down low-to-mid) together with a $216m litigation charge, and the stock fell 9.59%. 2026-07-23: the volume guide was unchanged with a 'low end' warning, but the GM floor was raised and marketing spend cut, and the stock rose 3.23%.

findings.finding: Arithmetic from the company's own documents: marketing spend (advertising, promotion and selling) rose $2.5m in Q1 and $26.2m in Q2, so $28.7m in H1. The FY guide was cut on 07-23 to $0-20m. H2 spend must therefore fall $8.7-28.7m YoY, about $0.60-2.00 per share after tax at a 29-30% tax rate on about 10.3m shares. Q3 is the larger-volume half of H2, so this is cost support for a beat against EPS consensus of $4.21-4.30 (Q3 2025: $4.25), even on weak volume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: EPS $4.25 against $3.34 (+27%), stock +5.45%. Q2 2026: EPS $3.65 against $4.83 (-24%) on a $26.2m spend step-up, stock still +3.23% on the spend cut and GM raise. The stock has reacted to the cost and guide story more than to the EPS line.

findings.finding: The Q3 shipments guide (down low to mid single digits, 07-23) runs against a very easy comparison: Q3 2025 shipments were -13.7% and revenue -11.2% to $537.5m. Consensus revenue of $523m (-2.6%) implies shipments of about -4% after 1-2% price. That is inside the company's guide, so the reported revenue line should land near the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue was in line ($568.3m against $566.7m) and the stock rose 3.23%. StockStory says SAM has missed revenue estimates several times over the past two years.

findings.finding: This is the first print under an interim CFO. Diego Reynoso resigned on 2026-08-17 (leaving 09-30). Matthew Murphy, the Chief Accounting Officer, has been interim Treasurer and CFO since 09-15 while a formal search runs, with a retention bonus of up to $700k. A finance chief in transition, setting the first 2027 colour, raises the odds of a conservative guide or a narrowing toward the low end.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Murphy was interim CFO from March to September 2023. No guidance-change reaction can be separated cleanly from that period in the baseline.
